kurz: Kostolany's change of hands, Marks' pendulum, and how much of a countercyclical purchase is left after tax and after your own behavioural mistakes.

bloecke.md:
Countercyclical investing relates to your own equity allocation. It is moved in the direction that the other investors are currently pulling out of. This does not require an opinion that goes against the majority. The definition is deliberately kept simple. A saver who keeps a savings plan running unchanged after a price slump buys more units for the same money and is thus acting countercyclically without making a forecast. Additional purchases strengthen the effect. Suspending the savings plan, on the other hand, is procyclical, even if it is meant as caution.

This must be distinguished from the contrarian in the narrower sense. The contrarian assumes that the prevailing opinion is wrong. The most precise objection to this stance was formulated by Howard Marks. In his view, doing the opposite of the majority is not what matters. What has to be checked is whether an opinion is already reflected in the price. An industry that is generally considered hopeless is therefore not in itself an argument for buying. It becomes one only when it is valued lower than its economic situation warrants.

## Kostolany's change of hands

Kostolany explained market phases in terms of the change of owners. His criterion is **trading volume** on the stock exchange. When prices and volumes rise sharply together, shares move from strong hands (hartgesottene Hände) into shaky hands (zittrige Hände). Kostolany calls this phase the exaggeration phase. When prices fall on high volume, the shaky hands give up and sell. The buying zone lies in this phase of capitulation. The criterion says nothing about the fair value of a company. It only shows who is selling at the moment and why.

Kostolany assigns investors to these groups according to his four Gs of the speculator, which he borrowed from a remark by Moltke about warfare: money (Geld), thoughts (Gedanken), patience (Geduld) and luck (Glück). By thoughts he means your own reasoning, that is, understanding what you are buying and why. Strong hands have all four Gs. Shaky hands lack at least one of the first three, that is, money, thoughts of their own or patience. They therefore sell at the wrong moment, regardless of how correct the analysis was.

punkte: Capital that will not be needed for several years, so neither a loan nor the emergency fund in the portfolio
Experience of at least one drawdown lived through personally, not just of charts showing one
Patience, even if the position stagnates for years
Own reasoning, written down in advance
Borrowed money or money earmarked for the short term
Entry in the late phase because others have made money
Reasoning taken from a video, a forum or a headline

bloecke.md: Kostolany's categories serve as a self-check. They do not provide a diagnosis of the market. An investor who has invested on credit, without a buffer and without written reasoning has shaky hands, regardless of how convinced they currently feel. More important than the question of where the market stands in the cycle is the question of whether you can withstand a further fall in prices without having to sell.

## Marks' pendulum and calibrating risk

Howard Marks describes the same movement with the image of a pendulum, but without Kostolany's anecdotes. Sentiment swings between greed and fear and between risk tolerance and risk aversion, and only rarely sits in the middle. His conclusion is deliberately modest. You cannot forecast the cycle, but you can assess where you currently stand and calibrate your own aggressiveness accordingly. This yields a rule for calibration, not a signal for the right moment (timing). The difference determines whether you stay fully invested or try to leave the market.

To assess where the market stands, the valuation level is more suitable than any survey. The Shiller CAPE smooths inflation-adjusted earnings over ten years and is therefore insensitive to profit cycles.

bloecke.titel: Shiller CAPE of the US stock market, 1995 to 2026
bloecke.unter: The CAPE fell from the dotcom peak to the low after the financial crisis and then rose again to the upper end of its historical range.

bloecke.md: The range is considerable. The CAPE stood at 43.77 in 2000, at 15.17 in 2009 and at 40.94 on 18 September 2026. The mean since 1900 is 17.42, the median 16.13. Two caveats apply to the interpretation, so that the CAPE is not misunderstood as a forecast. First, the CAPE has historically said little about the next one to two years. It correlates with long-term subsequent returns and not with performance in the next quarter. Second, all the values mentioned are US values. Reliable CAPE series for Germany and Europe were not available for this lesson, and a US value is not a verdict on a world ETF.

bloecke.unter: The gauge places the current CAPE within its range since 1900 and describes the situation without giving a forecast for the coming months.

## Sentiment indicators and the risk premium

There are numerous sentiment indicators, such as investor surveys, put-call ratios, volatility indices and fund inflows, and in Kostolany's case stock exchange trading volume. Their common problem is the threshold. In hindsight, you can always find a value beyond which “panic” prevailed. In advance, this value is not stable, because market structure and the group of participants change. Investors who use such indicators therefore have to set the threshold in writing beforehand. Otherwise you read into the curve whatever you wanted to do anyway.

The **implied equity risk premium**, by contrast, can be quantified well. It is backed out of current prices and expected cash flows and indicates what return above the risk-free rate the market currently demands for equity risk. It rises in phases of fear and falls in euphoria. It thus expresses market sentiment in percentage points.

bloecke.titel: Implied risk premium of the S&P 500 in selected years (Damodaran)
zeilen: late phase of the dotcom bull market
before the financial crisis came to a head

bloecke.md: In 1999, the market demanded around two percentage points above the risk-free rate for equity risk, in 2008 more than three times as much. A high premium is no guarantee of a successful purchase. It is the higher compensation for a risk that is very real at that moment. In 2008, the premium was high because a collapse of the banking system was conceivable. This is why buying countercyclically is uncomfortable. The higher premium compensates for a genuine danger and does not require other investors to be wrong.

## Buying in a crisis

A well-documented series shows how much the timing of entry matters. It is the S&P 500 index fund from Buffett's ten-year bet against five funds of hedge funds, with a starting value of 100 on 31 December 2007.

bloecke.titel: S&P 500 index fund from the Buffett bet, end of 2007 = 100
bloecke.unter: In the first year, the fund lost a third of its value, and money invested only after that had tripled by 2017.

bloecke.md:
An entry at the end of 2007 led to a level of 225.8 by the end of 2017, that is, a factor of 2.26 in ten years or around 8.5% a year.

An entry at the end of 2008 at 63 led to the same level of 225.8, that is, a factor of 3.58 in nine years or around 15.2% a year.

The difference of around 6.7 percentage points a year is due solely to the entry price. Conversely, getting from 63 back to 100 required +58.7%. Anyone who sold at the end of 2008 and only returned at the end of 2012 at 108.7 had realised the loss and bought back above the starting value.

The low can only be recognised in hindsight. The level of 63 was the year-end value for 2008; the low did not come until March 2009. Investors who bought in September 2008 because prices seemed “finally cheap” then experienced a further substantial decline. Countercyclical purchases are therefore spread over several tranches.

Buying more of an individual security is different from buying more of an index. A broad index recovers because it replaces its members. A single company cannot do that. Without a valuation judgement of your own, “averaging down” in an individual share is not a strategy. It amounts to refusing to admit a mistake.

## Hurdles in practice

The gap between the return of a fund and the return of its investors measures procyclical behaviour. Morningstar puts it at 1.2 percentage points a year for the decade to the end of 2025. It widens with volatility. Where countercyclical behaviour would pay off most, it is therefore sustained least often.

There is an objection to this measurement. The gaps arise from comparing money-weighted investor returns with time-weighted fund returns. With regular contributions, more money is invested later on, so the later years count for more in the money-weighted return. If their returns turn out lower than those of the earlier years, a difference arises without anyone having made a mistake. In the Financial Analysts Journal in 2026, Fulkerson, Jordan, Riley and Yan argue that poor timing costs considerably less than claimed.

The second hurdle is duration. The systematic form of countercyclical investing is the value approach. The cumulative value factor HML reached its high in December 2006 and lost 57.8% by September 2020. In July 2026 it is around 30% below the 2006 high and has thus been below that level for just over 19 years. The fact that two strong years followed in 2021 and 2022, with +22.2% and +31.7%, is of no use to investors who gave up in 2018. In addition, countercyclical investing is itself an active decision. Over ten years, only 11.9% of active European equity funds beat their passive counterpart.

## Tax rules in Germany

After tax, countercyclical investing looks different from how it looks in a backtest. Four points are decisive here.

First, the order of disposal is fixed. For units of the same kind in the same securities account, first in, first out applies without exception (Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG, the Income Tax Act). Investors who buy more cheaply after a crash and sell part of their holding years later are, for tax purposes, selling the oldest and usually cheapest units first. The taxable gain is therefore higher than you would intuitively expect.

Second, losses are offset in separate pots. Losses from capital assets can only be offset against income from capital assets (Section 20(6) sentence 1 EStG), and losses from share sales, more narrowly still, only against gains from share sales (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG). Anyone who realises a loss in a crisis in order to reallocate countercyclically should know which pot this loss ends up in. Across several banks, the pots can only be combined with a loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung), which must be applied for by 15 December (Section 43a(3) EStG).

Third, the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) is capped at the increase in value during the calendar year (Section 18(1) InvStG, the Investment Tax Act). It therefore does not apply in a loss year. In the crash year in which you buy countercyclically, there is thus no advance taxation. In addition, the 30% partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) is applied to the taxable income of an equity fund (Section 20 InvStG). The tax rate on the remaining part is 25% plus the solidarity surcharge, together 26.375%, plus church tax where applicable (Section 32d EStG).

Fourth, waiting has a cost. Interest on money held ready for buying in is fully taxable, that is, without partial exemption. It remains tax-free only within the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) EStG). Keeping liquidity ready for later purchases therefore costs more after tax than the gross calculation shows.

schritte.titel: Set the rule before prices fall
schritte.text: Set thresholds as the distance from the peak, for example −20%, −35% and −50%, and note a fixed amount with a date for each threshold. Rules that are written only after prices have fallen are not binding.

schritte.titel: Name the source of the money
schritte.text: Only use funds that will not be needed for several years, so no loan, no emergency fund and no amounts earmarked for the short term. Otherwise you are buying with shaky hands.

Without a valuation judgement of your own, choose a broad index instead of an individual security, and put the tranche in a separate sub-account so that the FIFO order does not worsen the later tax calculation.
On the day of purchase, write down what is expected and how an error would be recognisable. Only then can you check later whether the rule worked or chance did.

bloecke.md: In 1930, Kostolany became rich within a very short time by speculating on falling prices during the collapse of the Paris stock exchange. A year later, the Hoover Moratorium on German reparations cost him his entire fortune and left him in debt. He derived his rules from this loss, that is, from his own experience. He was right about the direction of his speculation and lost nonetheless, because leverage shortened the time he could hold out until his assessment was confirmed. Countercyclical investing and borrowed money therefore do not go together. Even if the position is right, the investor may be forced to give it up before it pays off.

mitnehmen: Acting countercyclically is a movement in the portfolio, not an opinion; simply continuing to buy after a price slump is countercyclical, even without any forecast.
According to Marks, what matters is whether the majority opinion is already reflected in the price, not whether the majority is wrong.
Valuation level and implied risk premium are measurable, sentiment surveys only seemingly so; thresholds for sentiment indicators must therefore be set in writing beforehand.
In the Buffett bet, the later entry yielded 15.2% instead of 8.5% a year, but the year-end level of 2008 was not the low, which is why countercyclical purchases should be made in tranches.
In Germany, the FIFO rule, the loss pots and the advance lump sum, which does not apply in a loss year, determine what is left of countercyclical purchases after tax.

begriffe.text: According to Kostolany, investors who lack at least one of the first three of his four Gs, that is, money, thoughts or patience. They buy in the exaggeration phase and sell in the panic.
According to Kostolany, investors who have all four of his Gs, that is, money, thoughts, patience and luck. This is why they can buy in the capitulation phase.
Return above the risk-free rate that the market demands for equity risk. It is backed out of current prices and expected cash flows, rises in crises and falls in phases of euphoria.
Gap between the return of a fund and the money-weighted return of its investors. It arises from the timing and size of deposits and withdrawals.
Tax rule under Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG according to which, for securities of the same kind in the same securities account, the units bought first are deemed to be sold first.
